title: Relative tensor pullback balanced naturality
statement: Let f:X → S be a scheme morphism, and let G be a functor on module sheaves whose objects and morphisms agree with the canonical tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Write R=f⁻¹O_S, H=restriction of scalars along R → O_X, and I=the canonical inverse-image module functor [def-pc-topological-inverse-image-module]. There is a family of isomorphisms of abelian sheaves e(M,N): underlying(M tensor over O_X G(N)) ≅ underlying(H(M) tensor over R I(N)), natural separately in every O_X-linear map M → M′ and every O_S-linear map N → N′. No additivity of G, flatness, nonzero-ring, boundedness, or derived-category assumption is required.

proof.text: Construct the R-linear inverse-direction map from the balanced pairing m,n to the image of m tensor sheafify(1 tensor n). Verify additivity, scalar compatibility and restriction compatibility directly. The sheaf tensor universal property supplies a unique map and its pure-tensor formula.

Prove simultaneous module-map naturality by precomposing with the pure-tensor inclusions; naturality of the tensor inclusion and of the extension sheafification unit identifies both composites. Apply the invertibility criterion to the constructed map.

Forget the R-module structure and invert the resulting isomorphism. Cancel its hom to turn the proved naturality equations into the required inverse-map equations. The hypotheses hG and hGmap give equality of G with tensorPullback by functor extensionality; substitute this equality.

proof_origin.reason: N4: explicit balanced pairing, unique sheaf tensor map, tensor-unit naturality and categorical inversion; invertibility alone split off.

lean.statement: theorem exists_relativeTensorPullback_balanced_natural {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace) ⥤ SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) (hG : ∀ M, G.obj M = Modules.tensorPullbackObj f M) (hGmap : ∀ {M N} (a : M ⟶ N), G.map a = eqToHom (hG M) ≫ Modules.tensorPullbackMap f a ≫ eqToHom (hG N).symm) : let R := ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing f.base S.sheaf)) let U := SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) let V := SheafOfModules.toSheaf R let H := SheafOfModules.restrictScalars ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map (Modules.tensorPullbackRingMap f)) let I := TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageModuleFunctor f.base S.sheaf let T := @curriedTensor _ _ (SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory X.sheaf) let T' := @curriedTensor _ _ (SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing f.base S.sheaf)) ∃ e : ∀ M N, U.obj ((T.obj M).obj (G.obj N)) ≅ V.obj ((T'.obj (H.obj M)).obj (I.obj N)), (∀ M M' (a : M ⟶ M') N, U.map ((T.map a).app (G.obj N)) ≫ (e M' N).hom = (e M N).hom ≫ V.map ((T'.map (H.map a)).app (I.obj N))) ∧ (∀ M N N' (b : N ⟶ N'), U.map ((T.obj M).map (G.map b)) ≫ (e M N').hom = (e M N).hom ≫ V.map ((T'.obj (H.obj M)).map (I.map b)))
